declarations.normative_text: A statement that changes what an operator or agent submits, refuses, trusts, retries, claims, or does when a capability is missing is behavior-deciding and belongs in this body.
References may elaborate a registered declaration or hold non-deciding measurements and examples; they must not be the only source of a behavior decision.

References use strict dialect version 1: only closed column-zero fences and valid same-line comments can exempt text; tabs, blockquotes, indented code, raw HTML, nested lists, and ambiguous structure are refused.
If shell or filesystem access is missing, report the exact blocked operation and request host-approved access; never fabricate output or weaken a trust boundary.
If Python or Git is missing, expose host-approved programs, preserve the repository working directory, and rerun.
Without Slurm, leave scheduler work blocked, retain the declared plan, and never infer a run result.
If Paseo or the bus is missing, do bounded local work without delegation or ask an operator to configure them; never create look-alike paths or daemons.
Without reviewers, retain the evidence and mark the change unreviewed; never borrow credentials or substitute worker self-confidence.
Without a tracker connector, retain the idempotent outbox intent as pending synchronization for an authorized session.
Never infer OpenCode or another worker backend merely because it loaded this skill.
Use `HANIG_SWARM_DIR` only to locate bundled programs; keep project, plan, state, input, and output paths relative to the project directory.
A `code` unit defaults to `codex/gpt-6-astra` with `thinking: high`; provider overrides must be declared on the unit.
Dispatch must refuse a mode unsupported by the selected provider; `mode` has no portable default.
Every `slurm` and `pipeline` unit must declare a runtime, using `runtime: none` as an explicit claim for a base-image-only unit.
Runtime availability must be established where the job lands by the declared canary or allocation-local preflight, never inferred from submit-host paths.
A unit cannot be its own canary; heterogeneous partitions, node-local paths, and run-time-built containers require allocation-local preflight.
A retry is a fresh empty attempt that redoes the whole unit; size units by maximum unrecoverable work and default `max_attempts` to 1.

`retry.mode: resume` is allowed only when a validated checkpoint survives the failed attempt, is made available to the new attempt, actually skips completed work, and still yields every declared output.
Declare restart exposure explicitly; the coordinator must not infer it from walltime, partition, `gpu_hours`, or DAG shape.
Bound concurrent filesystem load with plan-wide `max_running` and pools; `--max-new-dispatches` limits only one invocation.
Every attempt must receive an exclusive never-reused write root, and the worker writes only there; this is a trusted-writer convention, not an OS boundary.
A done predicate must include declared outputs, the coordinator-pinned pre-dispatch artifact basis, and kind-specific execution evidence; never replace isolation with observed attribution.
Missing pre-dispatch artifact basis fails closed; identical artifacts fail, while absent-then-present or changed artifacts satisfy only the production premise.
A container profile must expose exactly the attempt root as writable and declared inputs as read-only; ambiguous, shell-bearing, or silently weaker profiles are refused.
`os_enforced_isolation: true` requires the matching coordinator-held token and pinned direct-execution wrapper fact; backend and image must never be inferred.
Trust-deciding facts live in coordinator state outside operated worktrees and attempt roots; launch records and receipts are audit-only.
Closure is fixed by kind: `code` closes only on the matching merged PR, while `slurm` and `pipeline` close on predicate receipts; tracker and merge observations remain attested.
Code judgment must use the coordinator-anchored exact remote ref, route, base, and target; worktree-only commits, another ref, an unreadable route, or a local-only repository are refused.

Optional `scope` is a JSON list of repo-relative, case-sensitive fnmatch globs; absolute paths and '..' segments are refused, wildcards including ** span any depth, and [] allows no changed paths. Before merging, the orchestrator must run `scope-check PLAN --state-dir DIR --unit U [--json]` against the current attempt's launch-intent base and judged head from coordinator state only. Exit 0 means every changed path is in scope; exit 1 reports out-of-scope paths and separately deletions or rename-away paths; exit 2 is unchecked, including absent scope or judged head. Neither nonzero exit is a pass. This local, network-free advisory command changes no state or closure authority and never blocks advance.
Persisted judgment facts must retain their generation-specific rules and fail closed when that generation's anchors are absent; deleting coordinator state is not migration.
Verifier corpus admission protects only exact declared regular files and must refuse changed corpus entries, directories, globs, symlinks, gitlinks, or bounds violations.
Integration evidence must bind the produced head, target, unique merge base, candidate tree, verifier policy, and verifier digest; it supplements and never replaces merged-PR closure.
`write_scopes` constrains concurrently runnable plans but does not confine a process; each code attempt still needs its own verified linked worktree.
Code judgment must revalidate worktree, Git-directory, branch, ancestry, changed-tree, cleanliness, and inode facts before pinning the produced commit.
Crash recovery may adopt only a named agent or one unambiguous worktree matching the complete launch intent; workspace IDs are cleanup bookkeeping, never authority.

The coordinator must own each new code worktree and, before any cleanup, publish a complete base-bound snapshot only after tracked and untracked bytes pass content-digest and restore checks; preservation failure retains the worktree, and recovery material is audit-only rather than completion evidence or resume authority.
Outputs must be relative to the attempt run directory; paths resolving outside it are refused.
Move a queued job in place with `scontrol update`; never cancel and redispatch it because that loses the binding and changes the plan digest.

Plans are cluster-specific: lambda requires `--mem`, andromeda and chimera do not, partition names do not port, and planning must use current surveyed accounts, QoS, memory, partitions, home, and filesystem facts.
Use `chimera-login` rather than `chimera`, and do not decide whether to wait from `sbatch --test-only` estimates.
Test swarm changes on Python 3.10, not only the newest host.
Judge a pipeline only at the engine boundary; do not reimplement or claim judgment of its internal scheduler, tasks, retries, or intermediates.
If the surviving coordinator grows past roughly 300 lines or reacquires observed attribution, stop and revisit the design.
A lifted Slurm-module change must carry its callees, imports, and constants and run `tests/test_swarm.py::TestTheLiftIsClosed`.
Anything but `CONVERGED`, including `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, becomes `NEEDS_HUMAN`, closes no ticket, releases no dependent, cannot be promoted, and stays out of retries.
Read convergence criteria only from the frozen plan; validation must refuse misspelled keys before dispatch and forbid convergence blocks on `code`.
Run unattended advancement from a deterministic host scheduler, never a Paseo schedule or a fresh periodic LLM agent.
Use one coordinator node per plan with advisory `flock`; never add a heartbeat, TTL, or lock stealing.
Reconcile an unbound `swarm-<attempt>` through `squeue` and `sacct` before any resubmit.
After 600 seconds, `INCOMPLETE` must settle to terminal `FAILED_EVIDENCE` and hold dependents.
A canonical digest over dispatchable plan fields must refuse mid-flight edits.
Output claims arbitrate only coordinators sharing a run root; unknown liveness is never permission to release a claim and requires named operator intervention.
Code dispatch must refuse a non-empty shared Git stash; use a base read, patch file, or separate worktree and inspect status before committing.
Coordinator child filtering is an exact-name denylist, not general secret or worker credential isolation; daemon credentials and `HOME` remain outside it.
Worker authentication is not permission to call more models; widening access requires a designed proxy or named exception, while required branch-push and PR credentials are allowed.
LIMIT: One canary on one node at one time does not establish heterogeneous or node-local runtime availability; use allocation-local preflight.
LIMIT: Exclusive paths prevent accidental collision but not another same-UID writer.
LIMIT: The container profile restricts launched host binds, not the Unix principal, network, every descendant, or private scratch; tools needing writable host `$HOME` cannot use it.
LIMIT: Re-dispatch attempts without artifact basis; over 256 MB comparison uses size and mtime, and byte-identical regeneration is indistinguishable from no production.
LIMIT: Same-UID descendants can access authority through `/proc` or ptrace; only separate identities or an equivalent OS boundary close this.
LIMIT: No portable barrier proves every Paseo or Slurm descendant is dead; accepted receipts must record this limit.
LIMIT: The remote ref proves durable production on a preselected route, not authorship, correctness, review, merge, future reachability, or protection from another writer.
LIMIT: Only exact declared corpus files are protected; helpers, generated data, toolchains, configuration, and environment remain outside it.
LIMIT: Conflicts, moved targets, missing objects, ambiguous ancestry, and rebases make integration evidence unavailable.
LIMIT: `write_scopes` constrains the plan, not a process's writes.
LIMIT: Inodes detect path substitution, not Git-content tampering.
LIMIT: Exact environment filtering does not remove daemon-supplied credentials, files under `HOME`, or unknown names.
LIMIT: Registry checks reduce accidental adoption but cannot close the same-UID reserve-and-launch race.
LIMIT: A free-text workspace ID is cleanup bookkeeping only and cannot authenticate anything.
LIMIT: Only the workflow-engine boundary is judged; internal tasks and intermediates are not.
LIMIT: Plateau alone can converge at a bad value; pair it with a threshold when value matters.
LIMIT: Same-node `flock` trials do not certify NFS recovery or cross-node exclusion; use one coordinator node per plan.
LIMIT: Claims arbitrate only coordinators sharing one run root, persist beyond coordinator lifetime, and refuse release under unknown liveness.
LIMIT: Green at base and on the feature head says nothing about the eventual merged tree; integration testing is separate.
Swarm scripts require Python 3.8 or newer, use only the standard library, remain login-node safe, and keep network imports out of the coordinator.
